panels.shot: dramatic low-angle wide of Devagiri fortress gate at dusk
panels.action: Harapala stands in shadow before the looming walls of Devagiri, the rocky hill-fort rising behind him under a bruised purple sky, as armed horsemen approach from the plains below.

dialogue.text: In the dying years of the Khaljis, Harapala of Devagiri rose, rebelled, and met a punishment so brutal that his very skin became a warning at the gate.

i18n.hi: खिलजी सल्तनत के ढलते दिनों में देवगिरी के हरपाल उठे, बाग़ी बने, और ऐसी सज़ा पायी कि उनकी खाल ही फाटक पर चेतावनी बन गई।

panels.shot: high aerial wide over the plateau around Devagiri fort
panels.action: The hill of Devagiri rises stark from a dry plateau, its stone ramparts clinging to the rock as narrow paths wind upward; small clusters of houses dot the plains below.

dialogue.text: Devagiri, Yadava stronghold in the Deccan, had once defied Delhi. By 1311, its ruler Ramachandra bowed to Alauddin Khalji and lived as a vassal.

i18n.hi: दक्कन का यादव गढ़ देवगिरी कभी दिल्ली को ललकारता था। १३११ तक उसका शासक रामचंद्र अलाउद्दीन खिलजी के आगे झुक चुका था और जागीरदार बन कर जी रहा था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Ramachandra’s empty throne in Devagiri audience hall
panels.action: An ornate but austere stone throne sits vacant in a pillared hall, dust motes drifting in slanting light, a discarded Yadava banner folded on the floor.

dialogue.text: When Ramachandra died around 1311, he left a kingdom bent under Delhi’s tribute and a court where loyalty and resentment quietly wrestled for control.

i18n.hi: १३११ के आसपास रामचंद्र मरा, पीछे छोड़ गया ख़िराज के बोझ तले झुका राज और दरबार, जहाँ वफ़ादारी और रोष चुपचाप कुश्ती लड़ रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium wide of Malik Kafur’s army approaching Devagiri
panels.action: A disciplined Delhi cavalry column led by Malik Kafur rides toward Devagiri, banners snapping, armor glinting; the fort looms ahead under harsh sunlight.

dialogue.text: Ramachandra’s son Singhana III tried to break free. Malik Kafur answered rebellion with steel, killing Singhana in 1313 and tightening Delhi’s hold.

i18n.hi: रामचंद्र का बेटा सिंघना तृतीय आज़ाद होने को उठा। मालिक काफ़ूर ने बग़ावत का जवाब तलवार से दिया, १३१३ में सिंघना को मार डाला और दिल्ली की पकड़ कस दी।

panels.shot: three-quarter medium on Harapala in a dim chamber
panels.action: Harapala stands half-lit in a stone chamber, dressed in Yadava noble attire, brows furrowed, a rolled manuscript in hand, listening to distant drums of mustering troops.

dialogue.text: In the turmoil, another figure stepped forward: Harapala, Ramachandra’s son-in-law. The chronicles name him little, but place him at the heart of Devagiri’s last revolt.

i18n.hi: इस हलचल में एक और चेहरा आगे आया—हरपाल, रामचंद्र का दामाद। इतिहास कम बोलता है, मगर उसे देवगिरी की आखिरी बग़ावत के बीचोंबीच रखता है।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Harapala looking out from battlements
panels.action: Harapala stands on the battlements, gripping the parapet, gaze fixed on the plains below where scattered men gather with spears and mismatched armor.

dialogue.text: The succession crisis in distant Delhi after Alauddin’s death rippled outward. Harapala saw a narrow opening and tried to restore Yadava freedom.

i18n.hi: अलाउद्दीन की मौत के बाद दूर दिल्ली की ताज़पोशी की जंग की लहरें बाहर तक फैल गईं। हरपाल ने छोटी सी दरार देखी और यादव आज़ादी लौटाने की ठानी।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide of Harapala addressing a small group of retainers
panels.action: In a torchlit courtyard, Harapala faces a group of Yadava retainers, his hand clenched at his side, their faces tense, some hopeful, some fearful.

dialogue.speaker: harapala
dialogue.text: Delhi quakes. If we stand now, Devagiri may yet breathe free.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली डगमगा रही है। अगर अब खड़े हों, तो देवगिरी फिर सांस ले सकता है।

panels.shot: montage-style wide of skirmish outside Devagiri
panels.action: A tense tableau of two small forces clashing in the dust outside the fort: Yadava foot soldiers pressing forward against armored cavalry bearing the emblems of Delhi.

dialogue.text: Isami and Barani do not linger on battles. They simply record that Harapala rose in rebellion, and Delhi moved again to break Devagiri’s defiance.

i18n.hi: इसीमी और बरानी लड़ाइयों पर नहीं ठहरते। बस लिखते हैं कि हरपाल बग़ावत पर उठा, और दिल्ली फिर चली देवगिरी की सख़्त मज़बूती तोड़ने।

panels.shot: close-up on Harapala’s resolute face in the chaos
panels.action: Harapala, dust-streaked, stands amidst armed men on the ramparts as arrows arc through the air; his jaw is set, eyes hard, smoke hazing the sky.

dialogue.text: We do not know his words or his plans in detail. Only that he chose revolt, knowing what Malik Kafur had already done to Singhana III.

i18n.hi: हम उसके अल्फ़ाज़ नहीं जानते, न सारी तैयारियाँ। बस इतना कि उसने विद्रोह चुना, जानते हुए कि मालिक काफ़ूर सिंघना तृतीय के साथ क्या कर चुका था।

panels.shot: somber medium of Harapala bound and escorted by soldiers
panels.action: Harapala walks with hands bound, flanked by armored Delhi soldiers leading him down a stone passage; his face is calm, the men around him expressionless.

dialogue.text: Barani and Isami agree on the outcome. Harapala’s revolt failed. He was captured, a rebel prince in chains, delivered to the victors’ judgment.

i18n.hi: बरानी और इसीमी नतीजे पर एकमत हैं। हरपाल की बग़ावत नाकाम रही। वह पकड़ा गया, ज़ंजीरों में जकड़ा बाग़ी राजकुमार, फ़तह वालों की अदालत में घसीटा गया।

panels.shot: austere wide of an inner courtyard prepared for punishment
panels.action: An inner fort courtyard lies under gray sky, ringed by guards and officials; at its center, ominous instruments and a wooden frame stand starkly, shadows stretched long.

dialogue.text: The chronicles do not soften what followed. As punishment for rebellion, Harapala was ordered to be flayed alive, and his skin treated not as a body, but as a warning.

i18n.hi: इतिहास आगे की बातें नरम नहीं करता। बग़ावत की सज़ा में हुक्म हुआ—हरपाल की खाल ज़िंदा उतारी जाए, और उसके जिस्म की नहीं, उसकी खाल की नज़ीर बनाई जाए।

panels.shot: tight, symbolic shot on an empty gate arch of Devagiri
panels.action: The great stone arch of Devagiri’s main gate fills the frame, heavy wooden doors partly open, their iron studs catching harsh light; the image suggests absence and threat.

dialogue.text: Barani’s Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi and Isami’s Futuh-us-Salatin both state: Harapala’s skin was stuffed and hung at Devagiri’s gate, a brutal message to all who entered.

i18n.hi: बरानी की ‘तारीख़-ए-फ़िरोज़ शाही’ और इसीमी की ‘फ़तूह-उस-सलातीन’ दोनों लिखते हैं: हरपाल की खाल भर कर देवगिरी के फाटक पर टाँग दी गई, आने वालों के लिए बेरहमी का पैग़ाम।

panels.shot: wide shot of townsfolk passing under the gate, looking away
panels.action: Townspeople hurry beneath the looming gate, eyes downcast, bodies tense; armed guards stand nearby, watching the crowd and the road beyond.

dialogue.text: It was punitive statecraft, recorded without embellishment: a display meant to crush the thought of Yadava revolt, not a feud of faith, but a calculated terror of power.

i18n.hi: यह सज़ा से ज़्यादा हुकूमत की चाल थी, बिना सजावट के दर्ज: एक नुमाइश, ताकि यादव बग़ावत का ख़याल ही टूट जाए—यह मज़हबी जंग नहीं, ताक़त के खौफ़ की सोची‑समझी राजनीति थी।

panels.shot: broad aerial of Devagiri under new banners
panels.action: The fort of Devagiri is seen from above now bearing Delhi Sultanate banners atop its towers, the town below subdued, roads patrolled by cavalry.

dialogue.text: After Harapala, the Yadava line effectively ends in the record. Devagiri passes fully into Sultanate control, a Deccan outpost of Delhi’s expanding empire.

i18n.hi: हरपाल के बाद दर्ज इतिहास में यादव वंश लगभग ख़त्म हो जाता है। देवगिरी पूरी तरह सल्तनत के हाथ आता है, दिल्ली की फैलती सल्तनत का दक्कनी चौकीघर बन कर।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of Devagiri across changing skies
panels.action: The same fort is shown under shifting skies—clear blue, then monsoon clouds, then sunset—suggesting the passage of years as structures within the walls slowly change.

dialogue.text: Soon, other rulers will rise here. Devagiri will be renamed Daulatabad, and in later centuries it will see new faiths, new dynasties, new forced marches.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही यहाँ नए शासक उठेंगे। देवगिरी का नाम दौलताबाद होगा, और आने वाली सदियों में यह नई आस्थाएँ, नए वंश, नई जबरी यात्राएँ देखेगा।

panels.shot: gentle close-up of Harapala’s face in memory, fading into stone
panels.action: Harapala’s face appears ghostlike against the weathered stone of the fort, his features calm, then blend into the ancient rock, as if carved and eroding with time.

dialogue.text: Of Harapala himself, we know little beyond the bare lines of revolt and punishment. The chronicles leave him as a name at the hinge where Yadava rule snaps.

i18n.hi: हरपाल के बारे में हमें विद्रोह और सज़ा की सूखी पंक्तियों से ज़्यादा बहुत कम पता है। इतिहास उसे बस एक नाम छोड़ता है, उस जोड़ पर जहाँ यादव राज टूटता है।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Devagiri gate to the wider landscape
panels.action: The camera pulls away from the massive gate, revealing the fort, the surrounding fields, and distant hills, all quiet under a soft evening light.

dialogue.text: Harapala’s skin could be hung to end a kingdom, but not its memory. In that stark image at Devagiri’s gate, we still glimpse how power chooses to rule—and how resistance pays its price.

i18n.hi: हरपाल की खाल टाँग कर राज तो ख़त्म किया जा सकता था, याद नहीं। देवगिरी के फाटक की उस सख़्त तस्वीर में आज भी दिखता है कि हुकूमत कैसे राज करती है—और प्रतिरोध कैसे अपनी क़ीमत चुकाता है।
